8/The charges make about as much sense as the theory that the Southern Poverty Law Center paying informants for intel about hate groups is support for those groups. Here, DOJ will have to prove, beyond a reasonable doubt, that “86 47” conveys a physical threat against Trump. It's ambiguous at best.

7/The case against Comey is precisely the sort of political weaponization of the criminal justice system that this administration baselessly accuses the Biden administration of. Here are the 2 charges:

6/Later in the day Jim Comey was indicted—for the 2nd time—in a case that skates on even thinner ice than the one that was dismissed last year. The indictment is about this now-deleted Instagram post. DOJ says it's a threat of physical violence to the president of the United States. It sure looks like 1st Amendment-protected political speech, though.

5/DOJ moved to dismiss the case arguing she could only go to an executive branch agency—one impacted by Trump's firings—for relief, which of course, would have been a joke. On Tuesday a judge ruled she was entitled to go to fed'l court since Trump purported to fire her pursuant to Article 2 of the Constitution.

4/Former FBI Director Jim Comey’s daughter Maurene was the prosecutor who convicted Ghislaine Maxwell. Her performance was deemed “exemplary” until she was fired. She sued, arguing she was improperly removed because of who her Dad is, perceptions about her political affiliation, or both.

3/The motion in the ballroom case claimed that despite being asked by the military not to sue because of the “Top Secret nature of the important facility,” plaintiffs went ahead. Why? The motion explains: “This did not deter them because they suffer from Trump Derangement Syndrome, commonly referred to as TDS... & are represented by the lawyer for Barack Hussein Obama, Gregory Craig.” DOJ has become the president’s law firm.
